suggested_fixes: Make run_genus_mc.tcl derive TOP from top_module.txt when present (fallback to the current hardcoded value). Example pattern: set TOP [string trim [read [open "./top_module.txt" r]]] with existence checks; keep env override if you use one.

Optionally add a short comment in constraints/mc_genus.sdc documenting that txn_* ports are treated as synchronous single-cycle IO with 0 delay only for bring-up, and must be replaced with realistic interface constraints for signoff.
validation_ai_review.summary: Prep-contract looks complete and internally consistent: required artifacts exist (filelist, Tcl, SDC, README, top_module.txt), filelist resolves to existing RTL sources, selected top (ddr4_controller_top) is not a testbench/harness and has normal scalar/vector ports (no interface ports at the boundary), and dependency analysis shows no missing modules/files. Remaining items are non-blocking robustness/clarity improvements (TOP sourcing, generic SDC assumptions).
warnings: SDC is intentionally generic: it applies 0.0 input/output delays to all non-clock/non-reset ports. This is fine for bring-up but can mask real IO timing needs; treat mc_genus.sdc as a starter only (especially if any ports are meant to model an external DDR PHY/DRAM boundary).

run_genus_mc.tcl hardcodes set TOP "ddr4_controller_top" instead of reading top_module.txt. This is internally consistent with the current bundle (top_module.txt matches), but it is fragile if the top is overridden/regenerated later; prefer sourcing top_module.txt to keep artifacts coupled.

README_prepared.txt claims the flow 'preserves packages, interfaces' but this particular bundle contains no interface definitions/references. Not a problem—just note that interface-preservation is unexercised here.
Some modules include `timescale directives. Typically harmless for synthesis, but if your environment flags them, you may need to strip them in the generic sanitizer (non-blocking prep note).
